html:
The Easter Sunday bombings were suicide attacks on three churches and three luxury hotels in Sri Lanka on 21 April 2019, which killed more than 250 people.

The bombers belonged to a local Islamist group, and the Islamic State claimed the attack. Targets included St Anthony's Shrine in Colombo and St Sebastian's Church in Negombo, centres of the island's old Catholic community, a legacy of Portuguese times. Warnings from India had not been acted on.

After the attacks anger turned on Muslims, and fear helped elect Gotabaya Rajapaksa, defence secretary in the last years of the civil war, as president that November. His government's failures led to the crisis of 2022.
sum: The Easter Sunday bombings were suicide attacks on three churches and three luxury hotels in Sri Lanka on 21 April 2019, which killed more than 250 people.
